title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
A man obtained photographs from a woman's private social media accounts and used AI image-generation software to create sexually explicit images of her. He then distributed these fabricated images through multiple fake accounts across Instagram, Discord, and Facebook. This is a case of impersonation and non-consensual intimate imagery enabled by image synthesis technology deployed without any system to verify the purpose or consent of those whose likenesses were used.

The victim discovered the abuse only when third parties alerted her to the images circulating. Detection fell to the person being harmed rather than to any platform safeguard or filter. The police investigation traced the perpetrator through digital footprints across his fake profiles and recovered his devices. What is not established: whether the image-generation software had any built-in detection or blocking systems, or whether the social media platforms that hosted the content had mechanisms that could have identified and removed it earlier.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and spreading fake obscene images of a college acquaintance using artificial intelligence technology. Bansal, a BTech graduate in Electronics and Communication Engineering from East Punjabi Bagh, obtained photographs from the woman's private social media accounts and used AI image-generation software to create sexually explicit morphed images. He then distributed this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The victim, also 22 years old, discovered the abuse when she received messages from anonymous Instagram accounts alerting her to the fabricated images circulating on Discord servers. She reported the crime to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi, prompting an investigation that traced digital footprints across the fake profiles. During questioning, Bansal admitted knowing the woman from college and revealed that personal resentment between them had motivated his actions. Police recovered his mobile phone, SIM cards, and other digital evidence, and the investigation is ongoing.
title_en: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online
